title: Power struggle: Pinarayi finds Satheesan's role in power purchases 'mysterious', CM hits back
content: The LDF is in no mood to let the controversy surrounding the purchase of power from the 'over-the-counter' power platform, General Network Access (GNA), die down. Opposition Leader Pinarayi Vijayan called a press conference on Friday and said the agreement with GNA was an attempt to serve the interests of private companies that dominate power generation in the country. "GNA is not a power-producing company; it is only an over-the-counter platform. Why would the Chief Minister intervene directly on behalf of a company that does not produce electricity," Pinarayi said. The Opposition Leader wanted the government to name the private company whose power would be purchased through GNA. "It is highly mysterious that the name of the company is kept under wraps," he said. Pinarayi then urged Chief Minister V D Satheesan to publish all the files and documents related to the power purchase agreement with GNA. Soon after, the Chief Minister sought to rebut most of Pinarayi's charges in a Facebook post. He termed as "baseless" Pinarayi's remark that the "Chief Minister's interest in securing the deal for GNA is shrouded in mystery". Pinarayi: It is misleading for the CM to state that the power from Himachal Pradesh State Electricity Board was priced at 14.50 per unit. Not only did the HPSEB revise the cost to 12.50 per unit but also rescheduled the supply during peak hours. Chief Minister: This is incorrect. In the file that came to me, here is what the very officer you had called "efficient" (former KSEB chairman M D Rajamanickam) had said about Himachal power on October 29, 2026: "12.50/kWh shall not be treated as confirmed unless expressly accepted in writing by the competent HP (Himachal Pradesh) authority". It is clear from this that the Himachal authorities had not given KSEB an assurance that the cost would be reduced to 12.50 per unit. How did the Opposition Leader receive a proposal (of the lowering of cost) that even KSEB had not received? According to documents collected from KSEB and the Rajasthan Regulatory Commission, the Rajasthan board had approved an agreement to purchase electricity from Himachal on October 17, 2026, at Himachal's urgent request, and issued a letter on October 18. How can Himachal agree to supply electricity to Rajasthan at 15.50 per unit and offer it to KSEB at 12.50? Pinarayi: GNA's rate of 8.63 per unit will apply during the whole day, even during non-peak hours when Kerala does not require power. As a result, there will be an additional loss of 722 crore. The Chief Minister is masking this. He is trying to justify GNA offer by comparing it with the old rates of Himachal. CM: So, you have acknowledged that GNA is the better option when compared with Himachal's old tariff. Fact is, Himachal has offered KSEB only one rate. There is no distinction between an old rate and a new rate. Pinarayi Vijayan, who is now saying that GNA is not a power generation company, had purchased electricity several times through the same organisation when he was Chief Minister. Did those who prepared the note for the Leader of the Opposition deliberately forget this? If so, they are trying to embarrass you. We are ready to provide the details of the electricity purchased by the previous government through GNA if the Leader of the Opposition asks for them. Pinarayi: Why is there a reduction in Keralam's internal production? (Down to below 10 million units daily from over 20 MU in September). There is enough water in our reservoirs (65 per cent on November 5). There is power in the open market, too. The Chief Minister is manufacturing a power crisis with ulterior motives. CM: Let me bring to your attention what the former KSEB chairman wrote on October 29, 2026, in a file sent to the Chief Minister through the Electricity Minister: "An immediate decision is imperative, as the proposal has been under consideration for more than two weeks...
